name: Hamacho
tagline: Tokyo in 10 minutes and Otemachi in 15 minutes. Served by 1 line. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥130,000 to ¥140,000.
summary: The station is in Chuo City, served by Toei Shinjuku Line. Journey times to the main business districts are 15 minutes to Otemachi, 20 minutes to Shinjuku, 28 minutes to Shibuya and 25 minutes to Shinagawa. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥130,000 to ¥140,000. The station stands 1.8 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 2.4 m. The land around the station is close to level.

terrain.note: The station sits on the higher side of the ground around it, at 1.8 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from 0.7 m to 3.1 m, a difference of 2.4 m.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, the station itself falls inside the projected inundation area, to a projected depth of 0.5 to 3 m. All nine points within 400 m of the station fall inside the area too, and the deepest projection among them is 3 to 5 m. For storm surge, 7 of the nine points also fall inside the projected area. On the whole, the flood projection here is on the large side for the 23 wards.

medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station there are 11 clinics and 8 pharmacies. Day-to-day care is available close to the station. The nearest hospital is 山村病院, about 6 minutes' walk from the station. The next nearest is 湘南メディカル記念病院, about 15 minutes' walk. "Hospital" here means a facility OpenStreetMap records as one. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.
stationNote: 1 line serve the station: Toei Shinjuku Line.
congestion: Toei Shinjuku Line runs at 152% of capacity in the morning peak. The busiest stretch is 西大島→住吉, which this station is not on. At 150%, the ministry's scale describes shoulders not quite touching, with crowding near the doors. The figures describe each line's busiest stretch, so the stretch you ride may be easier.

rentRange.note: Around this station, One room ¥130,000 to ¥140,000 and 1K ¥130,000 to ¥140,000. 1LDK ¥200,000 to ¥210,000 and 2LDK ¥290,000 to ¥300,000. These are the per-station averages published by LIFULL HOME'S, Yahoo! Real Estate and at home, averaged together and rounded down to the nearest ¥10,000 (our own survey). All three are asking rents, so what tenants finally agree can be lower. Within the same station area the figure moves a great deal with the age of the building, the walk from the station, and whether the flat faces a main road.

rentReason: A one-room flat here goes for ¥130,000 to ¥140,000. Set against how long it takes to reach the central business districts, that is about average for the 23 wards. For 2LDK, though, the sources differ by ¥30,000 or more. They count different sets of properties, so read those figures as a range rather than a point.

neighbours.lead: Ningyocho is ahead on the number of lines and how close the centre is.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Hamacho. Ningyocho also has the Tokyo Metro Hibiya Line, Tokyo Metro Hanzomon Line and Toei Asakusa Line, which Hamacho does not. With more lines, Ningyocho is the better connected of the two. To Roppongi, for instance, Ningyocho is 12 minutes quicker. A one-room flat, though, costs about ¥5,000 more at Ningyocho.

neighbours.lead: Bakurocho is ahead on the number of lines and how close the centre is.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Hamacho. Bakurocho also has the JR Sobu Main Line and Toei Asakusa Line, which Hamacho does not. With more lines, Bakurocho is the better connected of the two. To Roppongi, for instance, Bakurocho is 7 minutes quicker. Rents, flood projections and the rest differ little.

goodFor: People commuting to Otemachi and Marunouchi
People who get around by bicycle or with a pushchair
People who want to finish their shopping on foot
notFor: People avoiding projected flood inundation areas
People who want another route when service is suspended
noiseSources: The 首都高速6号向島線 viaduct runs just outside the station. It is an expressway, so traffic is audible day and night

leads.terrain: The ground around the station is almost level, so you can choose where to live without thinking about slopes.
leads.groceries: There are 11 supermarkets within walking distance, and the nearest is 4 minutes on foot.
leads.hazards: The station itself sits inside the area projected to flood in the heaviest rainfall the government models.
leads.stationNote: Only the Toei Shinjuku Line serves this station, so when it stops you walk to another station.
leads.rentRange: The balance between commuting time and rent is about average for the 23 wards.
leads.medical: The number of clinics and pharmacies within walking distance is on the high side for the 23 wards.
leads.congestion: Morning loading on the lines here is about average for the 23 wards' stations.
leads.noiseSources: At this station, check the traffic noise before the noise people make.
